record.paper_title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev
record.original_question: In the general theory of orthogonal polynomials defined by Sobolev inner products that may include derivative-evaluation terms, determine which analytic properties of standard orthogonal polynomials are preserved, what algebraic properties the new polynomials have, whether a parallel Hilbert-space operator theory exists, and which Pade approximants are associated with these polynomials and how those approximants behave.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu_0, \mu_1, \dots, \mu_m$ be (possibly signed or discrete) Borel measures on the real line, and let $\{c_{j,k}\}$ be a finite collection of real coefficients with associated points $\{x_{j,k}\} \subset \mathbb{R}$. Define a Sobolev-type inner product on the space of real polynomials by
$$\langle p, q\rangle_S \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{m} \int_{\mathbb{R}} p^{(k)}(x)\, q^{(k)}(x)\, d\mu_k(x) \;+\; \sum_{j,k} c_{j,k}\, p^{(k)}(x_{j,k})\, q^{(k)}(x_{j,k}),$$
and let $\{S_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ denote the corresponding sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials (assumed to exist and be unique). Investigate the following four questions for general families of such inner products:

(a) Analytic properties. Which analytic properties of standard orthogonal polynomials (asymptotic behavior on and off the support, $n$th-root and strong asymptotics, location and limiting distribution of zeros, Mehler–Heine type formulas, convergence and summability of associated Fourier expansions) carry over to the polynomials $\{S_n\}$, and under what conditions on the measures and derivative-evaluation terms?

(b) Algebraic properties. What algebraic relations (recurrence relations replacing the three-term recurrence, Christoffel–Darboux type kernels, differential or difference equations, ladder operators, connection formulas) are satisfied by $\{S_n\}$?

(c) Operator theory. Does there exist a parallel Hilbert-space operator theory: a natural self-adjoint or symmetric operator on a suitable Hilbert space completion of the polynomials whose spectral analysis encodes $\{S_n\}$, analogous to the role of the Jacobi matrix and multiplication operator in the classical theory?

(d) Padé approximation. Which Padé (or multipoint Padé / Hermite–Padé) approximants are naturally associated with $\{S_n\}$ and the Cauchy/Stieltjes transforms of the measures $\mu_k$, and what are their convergence, error, and pole-distribution properties?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on Sobolev orthogonal polynomials emphasize that general analytic, algebraic, operator-theoretic and Padé-approximation aspects remain active areas with major unresolved problems. In particular, the lack of a three-term recurrence and Christoffel–Darboux formula in the Sobolev setting, the non-symmetry of the multiplication operator, and the convergence of Sobolev–Fourier expansions are explicitly identified as open problems in current literature.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal Polynomials and Operator Theory. Open Problems and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: analyzes symmetric operators associated with a Sobolev type inner product, pointing out connections between Cholesky factorization and UL factorization of shifted Jacobi matrices
status_evidence.claim: Operator-theoretic aspects of Sobolev inner products are still under active investigation as open problems.

status_evidence.title: On Sobolev orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: In the Sobolev setting, the multiplication operator is no longer symmetric and the three-term relation no longer holds; convergence of Fourier expansions in Sobolev orthogonal polynomials has not been resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Key algebraic and analytic questions for Sobolev OPs remain open.
